title.narrative: Promoting Early Advancement Through Childhood Education (PEACE)

description.narrative: The PEACE [Promoting Early Advancement Through Childhood Education] Project is a newly launched initiative by Slum2School Africa aimed at tackling Nigeria’s education and early learning crisis through an innovative, inclusive, and scalable model for children aged 2 to 11 in underserved communities. Implemented across 6 states (Abuja, Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Ebonyi and Rivers) in Nigeria’s 6 geopolitical zones, the project seeks to close the education equity gap by integrating Early Childhood Education Centers and Maker Spaces, digital/hybrid learning tools, and teacher development into public and community schools. Through experiential, play-based education, the initiative fosters foundational literacy, numeracy, creativity, and socio-emotional skills—positioning children for long-term success. Over the next phase, 12 ECE Centers and Maker Spaces will be established to provide safe, tech-enabled learning environments in rural and urban low-income areas. Each year, 600 teachers will be trained as ECE Accelerators, enhancing their capacity to deliver inclusive, child-centered learning to 18,000 children annually across 50 schools. By 2030, the program aims to reach over 2 million children, making it one of Nigeria’s largest grassroots-driven ECE efforts. Aligned with SDG 4, PEACE is designed to be scalable, replicable, and transformative—ensuring that every child, regardless of background, can thrive through quality early education.
